en.title: New Resident Evil Movie Shatters Franchise Box Office Record
en.summary: The latest Resident Evil film has achieved a monumental feat, surpassing all previous entries in franchise history. This critical and commercial success marks a significant turning point for the long-running series.
en.body:
The latest cinematic outing for **Resident Evil** has achieved a remarkable milestone, demolishing previous franchise records at the global box office. In just its second weekend of release, the film has officially crossed the $100 million mark domestically. This impressive figure not only signifies a massive win for the film itself but also sets a new benchmark for the entire **Resident Evil** movie saga. Prior to this, the highest-grossing film in the series domestically was 2010's **Resident Evil: Afterlife**, which garnered approximately $60 million. The current film's momentum suggests it has a real chance to challenge the global record holder, **Resident Evil: The Final Chapter**, which earned a total of $312 million worldwide.

Globally, the new **Resident Evil** movie has already amassed an impressive $196.5 million against a reported $75 million production budget. This performance stands in stark contrast to some of the franchise's more recent theatrical attempts. For instance, 2021's **Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City**, directed by Johannes Roberts, only managed to bring in $17 million domestically. Following that film's disappointing performance, rights-holder Constantin Film reportedly placed the franchise on hiatus. It wasn't until director Zach Cregger presented a compelling new vision that the series was revived for the big screen. Cregger's film, which has been met with widespread acclaim, is now proving that a fresh perspective can lead to unprecedented commercial success for the brand.

## A New Era for Resident Evil Cinema

The success of this latest **Resident Evil** film is particularly noteworthy given the franchise's history. While Paul W.S. Anderson's six films, starring Milla Jovovich, collectively earned over $1 billion worldwide, they often faced criticism for both commercial and critical shortcomings. This new film, however, seems to have struck a chord with audiences by balancing thrilling action with a more cohesive narrative. The strong box office performance suggests that fans are eager for a more nuanced and engaging adaptation of the beloved survival horror game series. This renewed enthusiasm could very well pave the way for future installments, reigniting interest in the zombie-infested world that has captivated gamers for decades.

## What's Next for the Franchise?

With such a resounding success, the question on everyone's mind is whether a sequel is on the horizon. Director Zach Cregger has expressed that he has ideas for where the story could go next, though he has also indicated a potential reluctance to direct further franchise films. Details regarding any potential follow-up, including a release date or further casting information, have not yet been announced. Fans will be eagerly awaiting any official word from Constantin Film as this new chapter in the **Resident Evil** cinematic universe unfolds.

Fans are clearly responding positively to Cregger's vision, with the film's box office performance speaking volumes about the appetite for quality horror. This isn't just a win for the movie; it's a win for the **Resident Evil** brand as a whole, proving that with the right creative approach, the franchise can still dominate both the gaming and film industries.

content_raw: Zach Cregger's highly acclaimed Resident Evil movie had another strong showing at the box office for its second weekend, propelling the film to break another franchise record. It already broke the record for biggest opening weekend for the franchise , and now the movie has made more than $100 million domestically. That's a new record for the franchise--before this, the biggest success domestically for the franchise was 2010's Resident Evil: Afterlife ($60 million). Globally, Resident Evil has now made $196.5 million against a reported $75 million production budget (not counting marketing costs). The highest-grossing Resident Evil movie globally is Resident Evil: The Final Chapter, which made $312 million worldwide. Time will tell if 2026's Resident Evil will catch up. Check out the list below to see how the other mainstream theatrical Resident Evil movies did at the domestic box office. Director Paul W.S. Anderson made six Resident Evil movies that starred his wife, Milla Jovovich, and while none of them individually did very well commercially or critically, they combined to earn over $1 billion worldwide. The worst-performing theatrical Resident Evil movie was 2021's Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City, which made just $17 million domestically. It was directed by Johannes Roberts and starred Kaya Scodelario as Claire Redfield and Avan Jogia as Leon S. Kennedy. After that film disappointed, rights-owner Constantin put the franchise on hiatus and planned to keep it on ice until Cregger came to the company with a pitch for Resident Evil . His movie is doing great, so people are wondering if there will be a sequel. That remains to be seen, and while Cregger has said he has ideas for where they story could go next , he's also said he is finished with franchise movies . The Resident Evil movie is a huge success, but the recent lift in sales of games in the series is not completely attributable to that, according to a research firm.
